subject: Subprocessor disclosure for Pacific Bank - DDQ
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@pacificbank.com>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: Pacific Bank InfoSec <infosec@pacificbank.com>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Subprocessor roster & data flow map for DDQ

Hi Rishi,

Thanks for the conversation yesterday. As part of our procurement DDQ and InfoSec review we need a full current list of Redwood's subprocessors (including vendors used by your CDN/observability/telemetry partners), the countries where they process/transit data, and whether customer data is persisted by each vendor. Our legal team also wants to understand which subprocessors handle any production PII/tokens, and whether any of them are outside the US or EU.

Can you send the roster and a simple data flow map (or a link to a document) by end of week? Also note we may request exported evidence for SOC2 or encryption keys handling later — we'll flag specific asks in follow-ups.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Pacific Bank is on a tight timeline.

Best,
Sarah Lin
Senior Vendor Risk Analyst
Pacific Bank

--
Pacific Bank InfoSec: infosec@pacificbank.com
From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah.lin@pacificbank.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster & data flow map for DDQ

Sarah —

Thanks for the note and the timeline. We're happy to share our subprocessor roster and an annotated high-level data flow. I've looped in Kimberly (privacy & compliance) and Marissa (partner ops) so we can ensure the export includes the jurisdiction and persistence flags you asked for.

Quick clarifications we typically provide in these packets:
- Vendor role (e.g., CDN, telemetry, KMS, metrics, observability)
- Primary processing countries and any transient transit locations
- Whether customer data is persisted, cached (TTL), or only transient in memory
- Whether the subprocessor has access to customer plaintext or only hashed/telemetry aggregates

We'll attach our current roster XLSX and a guidance note for your legal team. If you prefer, we can also produce a redacted export that flags only the items relevant to Pacific Bank's DDQ (e.g., PII access).

Expecting to send the first draft by tomorrow EOD. If your team has a template/format (CSV column names or a specific DDQ), please send it and we'll map to it.

Thanks —
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachments: pacificbank_ddq_submission_guidance.pdf (planned)
From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Subprocessor roster & data flow map for DDQ

Folks —

I've drafted the subprocessor roster and annotated the persistence/access columns. Key calls-outs:
- CDN provider (EdgeWave) — transit in US, EU; does not persist customer payloads beyond short cache TTLs unless configured by the customer.
- Observability (StreamSight) — retains telemetry logs (IP+request metadata) for 90 days; hosted in US and GCP EU region for EU customers.
- Telemetry relay (RelayBridge) — transient forwarding, but retains delivery logs for 14 days; no plaintext customer content persisted.
- KMS/HSM (KeyVaultCo) — customer keys are managed via HSM in US region; access logs retained and available on request.

I've attached the roster (redwood_subprocessors_2026-07.xlsx) and a short guidance PDF for legal (pacificbank_ddq_submission_guidance.pdf). I also flagged three subprocessors that require an export of additional evidence if the customer requests (SOC2 reports and network diagrams).

Notes on cross-border: any transit through edge POPs in APAC is purely transient (TCP routing) and does not store tokens; Europe-anchored tenants are served from EU GCP regions where possible.

Open questions to confirm before we send externally:
1) Do they want per-environment (prod/staging) differentiation?
2) Is Pacific Bank requesting raw access logs for the telemetry vendor or only processed metrics?

If we don't hear back by EOD we'll send the roster with the above caveats and offer to provide the additional evidence under NDA/PIA request.

—Kimberly
Director, Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_subprocessors_2026-07.xlsx

Subject: Subprocessor roster and data flow map (attached)

Hi Sarah —

Attached is the subprocessor roster you requested (redwood_subprocessors_2026-07.xlsx) and a short guidance note for your legal team (pacificbank_ddq_submission_guidance.pdf). High-level summary below:

- We have included vendor role, processing/transit countries, persistence flags (persisted/cache/transient), and whether the vendor may access plaintext customer content.
- Three subprocessors are noted as requiring evidence (SOC2/network diagram/KMS attestation). If Pacific Bank would like those, we can share under our standard evidence request process — we usually route that through a secure Drive folder and a signed NDA or data processing addendum amendment.
- For EU-anchored customers we can provide EU-only hosting options for certain services; Pacific Bank's security team can specify residency requirements and we'll map available configurations.

Next steps: please confirm whether you want (A) a simple roster only, (B) roster + SOC2 evidence for flagged vendors, or (C) roster + full telemetry export (requires additional approvals). I'll coordinate the evidence pulls once you confirm.

Link to the HubSpot deal and evidence folder so your procurement team can reference: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/deal/DEAL-58432 and https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aB_example_subprocessor_evidence

Happy to jump on a quick call with InfoSec to walk through the items — propose Tue Jul 6 10:00 PT if that works.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference
